title: Token Pathway Wireflow & Grooming — Storyboard Draft
content:
Purpose:
This document captures a first-pass storyboard + wireflow for a token-level cost & latency exploration surface that surfaces request "pathways" — per-invocation token progression mapped to cost slices, latency contributors, and model/runtime events (batch boundary, cache hit/miss, fallback). The aim is to propose an interaction that helps engineers and product owners trace a single invocation from entry -> token emission and quickly identify the dominant cost/latency factors.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce mean time to root cause for expensive invocations from >1 day to <4 hours for on-call/eng.
- Provide an at-a-glance signal for invocation health by combining cost+latency anomalies into three colored lanes (green/amber/red).
- Enable click-to-inspect: from an invocation row to token timeline to model variant pivots (can re-run at lower quality for repro).

Primary personas:
- Backend engineer (platform): wants to know whether a spike is due to batching, KV cache misses, or model selection.
- ML engineer (inference): wants token-level latency distribution and quantization/variant impact.
- Product manager (mobile app): focused on cost tradeoffs and whether a change to prompt length vs model variant is warranted.

Constraints / Design guardrails:
- Must not surface PII or user prompt content in plain text in shared views (use redaction toggles / hashed placeholders).
- UI should be performant for lists of invocations (support server-side pagination and sampling).
- Keep primary view mobile-compatible but optimized for desktop (two-column): left list of invocations, right detail pane with token-pathway.

High-level interaction flow (wireflow steps):
1) Invocation list (default): sortable table (time, route, model, tokens, total cost, total latency, health badge). Each row has quick actions: Open Pathway, Create Incident, Compare With Baseline.
2) Open Pathway -> Right pane slides in with header: invocation metadata + timeline scrubber.
3) Token Pathway canvas: horizontal time axis. Each token rendered as a thin vertical bar positioned at emission time, colored by latency bucket and stacked with small colored strip for cost slice (inferred/calc). Hover shows token tooltip: index, token text preview (redacted), token latency (ms), cost cents, runtime event markers (batch-start/batch-end/cache-hit/fallback).
4) Waterfall lanes beneath canvas: Runtime events lane (GPUs, queue delay), Model lane (variant name + quantization flag), Network lane (egress latency to KMS if signing), and Cost attribution lane (batch amortized, compute, kv-cache benefit).
5) Quick actions in pane header: Re-run with args (simulate lower temperature/quantize), Toggle redaction, Export token timeline (CSV), Create evaluation prompt set from this invocation.

Low-fi ascii wireframe (rough):
[Invocations list | Pathway pane]
[time | route | model | tokens | cost | latency | health] [>>]
----------|------------------------------------|--------------------------------
Pathway pane
-------------------------------------------------------------
Invocation header: route / user / id / model v / total tokens / total cost / total latency
[ scrubber ] [play animation] [export] [redact toggle]
Token canvas: 0ms -------------------------------------------------> 2500ms
| | | | | each vertical bar = token (color: latency bucket)

Waterfall lanes below (small stacked rows):
- Runtime queue |■■■■■■■■■-----
- GPU compute  |-----■■■■■■■■■--
- KV cache hit |--X--X-------X----- (X = cache hit)
- Model variant| v1.2-q8 -> fallback-> v1.1-fp16
- Cost comp.   | compute | decoding | overhead

Key components to design and backend needs:
- Token timeline calculation: requires per-token emission timestamp, per-token latency (decode time) and event markers. Backend must persist per-invocation token traces for sampled invocations only (configurable retention).
- Cost attribution engine: map token decode time to compute-seconds and cost model per instance type, include batching amortization logic.
- Redaction service: server-side redaction pipeline that keeps token position and hashed token placeholder when toggled.
- Re-run simulator: lightweight sandbox that can replay prompt with alternate config (quantize, batch size, model variant) to estimate cost/latency delta (not a real inference run, just estimator).

Metrics to surface in header and CTA rules:
- Total tokens, generated tokens, prompt tokens (if available), total cost (USD), total latency (ms), batch size at emission peaks, peak concurrent requests in window.
- Health heuristics: if cost/token > P95 baseline * 2 OR latency > SLO*1.5 mark amber; if both mark red.

Backlog / grooming tickets (draft priorities):
- CONSOLE-1976: "Invocation pathway pane — wireframes and acceptance" (3 pts) - Provide the pane skeleton + scrubber + token canvas. Owner: Asha.
- RI-1423: "Trace ingestion: per-token event schema and retention" (5 pts) - Add new DB tables + sampling policy. Owner: Brian.
- UX-4012: "Redaction toggle and permissions model" (2 pts) - Determine RBAC, implement masked preview. Owner: Lena.
- CONSOLE-2001: "Estimator service for re-run simulator" (8 pts) - Cost/latency model; safe-mode simulator API. Owner: Sofia.
- CONSOLE-2002: "CSV exporter + quick incident creation" (1 pt) - small button and webhook. Owner: Asha.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP):
- Open Pathway shows token timeline for sampled invocations within 1s of click on list for pages with <=50 rows.
- Hovering tokens shows a tooltip with token index, latency, and cost. No raw prompt text unless redaction is off and viewer has permission.
- Backend can store and return per-token traces for sampled invocations at 1% sampling rate and configurable TTL.
- Health badge logic implemented and visible in invocation list with click-to-filter on badge state.

Open questions & risks:
- Storage cost: raw per-token traces have high cardinality. Need retention policy, sampling guidance, and compression plan.
- Privacy: how do we handle prompt text that may contain PII? Default must be masked; opt-in audit log required for unmasked views.
- Performance: rendering thousands of tokens in the browser might be slow — need to implement canvas virtualization and progressive rendering.
- Estimator accuracy: simulator may mislead users if estimates have high error; must surface confidence interval.

Design alternatives we considered briefly:
- Sparklines-only approach: show cost+latency sparkline per invocation and expand to a separate full-page timeline. Pros: lighter initial UI. Cons: harder to correlate token events across lanes.
- Bucketed tokens (group tokens into buckets of N tokens): reduces visual noise but loses per-token granularity. Could be fallback for long outputs.

Next steps (this week):
- Sync with infra on trace schema + retention (Brian) — due 2025-11-24.
- Quick paper prototype in Figma for the token canvas interactions (Sofia) — due 2025-11-21.
- Create the CONSOLE-1976 ticket with acceptance criteria and attach this doc (Asha) — done (draft).
- Schedule 30m grooming session with SRE, serving-runtime, and product on 2025-11-26.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally exploratory: focusing on the mental model of a token as the unit of cost/latency attribution rather than jump straight to aggregated charts. Please flag any privacy/regulatory concerns early.
- Look for gaps in the estimator assumptions — we will draft a short spec for the estimator math separate from the UI.

Attachments / references:
- Figma prototype (draft): https://figma.redwood.com/file/ABCD1234/token-pathway-v1
- Jira epic: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CONSOLE-1976
- Trace schema proposal: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Token+Trace+Schema (draft)

-- end of draft --
